_doc: Human criterion, versioned (E9, realism batch). Each theme is one instruction the professional gives, with the
regular expression that recognises it in ANY of his wordings. build_canonical_notes.py measures the support of each theme
over the corpus and picks its canonical wording; compose_notes then consensuses over THEMES instead of over literal strings.
Why it is needed: he writes the hydration line in 636 of 1.033 diets across 357 distinct strings, and NOT ONE string in the
whole corpus reaches the consensus threshold note_t = 0,35. Consensus over text could never see an instruction he always gives.
The patterns are deliberately generous inside a theme and disjoint between themes; a note may legitimately match two themes
(«no tomar postres, ni azúcar, ni bebidas alcohólicas» is sugar AND alcohol) and then both are supported.
rule_ids links a theme to the rules of the constitution it makes evaluable, so a note-level rule can be satisfied by the
canonical wording instead of by a copied sentence.

must_match: the canonical wording is chosen among the wordings that satisfy this regex — the note pattern of the rule the theme claims to make evaluable. Without it the most frequent wording can be one the rule engine does not recognise: the hydration canonical was «HAY QUE BEBER AUNQUE NO SE TENGA SED…», which carries the instruction but does not match «beber agua|litros de agua», and agua_2.5L scored 0,019 instead of ~0,79.
NOT notes: section headers the document parser kept, and fragments of the contact footer. 639 occurrences, 14,5 % of the
field. They were being emitted into proposals — 'Observaciones:' reached a golden snapshot before this filter existed.

themes.pattern: litros de agua|ingesta de agua|beber agua|beber.{0,20}litros|tragos peque|aunque no se tenga sed|hidrataci[oó]n|entre comidas.{0,30}beber|no beber (mucho|mucha cantidad)
no tomar postres|evitar el az[uú]car|evitar az[uú]car|nada de az[uú]car|sin az[uú]car añadid|harinas blancas|cereales en caja|dulces

themes._doc: shares its most frequent wording with evitar_azucar_y_postres; compose_notes emits each canonical text once
